reason: The immediate goal is to build the bed structure, so placing the steel on the growing-room floor seems useful.
expectation: I expect a frame or support for the beds, though it may need further fittings.

alternatives.reason: The hose and pump should help with irrigation, but the bed structure is the current goal.

effect: The raised frames define separate crop beds and leave room for the reservoir beneath their outlets.
reaction: The different bed depths make the structure feel purposeful.
reason: Lining the frames is a practical next step toward completing the shared beds.
expectation: I expect the food-safe sheet to line the beds, though irrigation will still need attention.

alternatives.reason: The pump and hose are needed for irrigation, but I want to finish the beds first.

effect: The beds are lined and their drains sealed; irrigation remains to be connected.
reaction: The distinction between the frame carrying the load and the liner holding solution makes sense.
reason: Connecting the hose to the reservoir and pump seems like a useful step toward circulating water through the beds.
expectation: I expect an irrigation supply assembly that can later connect to the beds, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the hose directly to the beds also seems useful, but I want to prepare the pump first.

effect: The reservoir now has an aerating return and a pump positioned to recirculate solution; it still needs to connect to the beds.
reaction: The falling return stream provides a clear purpose for aeration.
reason: Connecting the hose to the lined beds is the only offered gameplay action and should advance the irrigation setup.
expectation: I expect the hose to connect the beds to the irrigation system, though further assembly may be needed.

effect: The beds now drain toward the reservoir, and the next goal is to complete the return circuit.
reaction: The sloped drains have a clear purpose in preventing water from pooling around the roots.
reason: Joining the reservoir to the drained beds is the only offered gameplay action and directly serves the new goal.
expectation: I expect the beds and reservoir to form a recirculating irrigation system, though it may still need water or other fittings.

effect: The beds and reservoir now form a shared distribution and return system with separate root-zone adjustments; both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The shared pump with individual flow adjustments is a satisfying practical detail, though the beds remain empty.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the aerating reservoir was most worthwhile: the falling return stream gave the assembly a clear physical purpose and explained how the solution is recirculated.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the drains was sensible but less engaging as the only offered action, following several similar assembly steps.

surprise.text: The return hose aerates the solution by letting it fall into the reservoir; I had expected a more generic pump-and-hose assembly.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The liner, sloped drains and reservoir each had an explained purpose, although the compatible-option menu did not require me to discover those connections.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see the empty beds become a working growing system, especially if the next chapter explains the crops' different needs; this chapter's physical details made the setup worthwhile.
